subject: RFI: Data sovereignty & international transfers — ZionCare operations
messages:
From: Emily Roberts <emily.roberts@zioncare.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: privacy@zioncare.com; marco.alvarez@zioncare.com
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 16:13:00 -0400
Subject: RFI: Data sovereignty and international transfers — ZionCare

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking our call this morning. As discussed, ZionCare is compiling an RFP packet for a platform to process protected health-related text and metadata across our EU clinics and US HQ. We need a consolidated response covering:

- Data residency / sovereignty controls and options for EU-hosted processing or contractual alternatives.
- Which cross-border mechanisms you support (SCCs, DPF, BCRs) and any limitations for healthcare data.
- A list of subprocessors and whether any processing occurs in APAC/US/EU regions.
- Technical evidence: encryption at rest/in transit, KMS key lifecycle, audit logs retention, and network egress controls.
- A draft DPA annex (if available) and timeline for execution.

Please see our attached question set (zioncare_rfi_questions.pdf) for specifics — we’d appreciate a response by EOD Oct 6 so our procurement can advance before the board review. If anything needs clarification, we can schedule a short follow-up.

Best,
Emily Roberts
Head of Vendor Risk — ZionCare

Attachment: zioncare_rfi_questions.pdf
From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
To: Emily Roberts <emily.roberts@zioncare.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Data sovereignty & international transfers — ZionCare

Emily — thanks for the detailed packet and for outlining the timeline. We're happy to respond and will compile a single evidence pack that maps to each numbered question in your PDF.

Quick clarifying points to ensure alignment:
1) Is the scope limited to PHI-like text and metadata generated inside the EU clinical sites, or do you expect Redwood to process EU-origin patient data routed via US-based systems?
2) Are you open to Redwood using the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) as an operational transfer mechanism for subsets of telemetry and non-identifiers, or do you require SCCs for all patient-level processing?
3) Do you need our full subprocessor roster or just the subset involved in inference and logging?

I've attached a preliminary dataflow CSV (redwood_initial_dataflow.csv) to show the default processing path and regions — this is a starting point and we'll expand it into the complete evidence pack.

We can deliver the consolidated response and a draft DPA annex by Wednesday, Oct 6 (EOD) as requested. If helpful, Marissa and Laura will join the call next week to walk through technical evidence.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_initial_dataflow.csv
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai, Emily Roberts <emily.roberts@zioncare.com>

Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Data sovereignty & international transfers — ZionCare

Adding a few technical notes and the internal checklist we'll include in the packet:

- Encryption: AES-256 at rest (cloud KMS) and TLS1.3 in transit. We will include KMS key rotation policy (90-day rotation for tenant keys; CMK rotation cadence in evidence).
- Key management: integration with customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) available for Dedicated & Private deployments; hosted mode uses Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed root keys.
- Auditing: per-request tracing (request_id) and token-level billing logs retained 365 days by default; extended retention options available for enterprise contracts.
- Subprocessors: inference compute (partner GPU provider), logging/metrics provider, and object storage provider. We'll prepare the full roster and regional footprints.
- Certifications: SOC2 Type II (controls report), penetration testing summary, and our compliance runbook excerpt.

I'm attaching the internal evidence archive (internal_evidence_pack.zip) — this contains snippets we will convert into client-facing PDFs. Plan: Soojin to review legal phrasing; Lauran to validate mapping for the clinical flows.

-Marissa
Senior Security & Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: internal_evidence_pack.zip

Thanks, Soojin and Marissa — this is very helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side before you finalize:

- For patient-level processing that includes identifiers, ZionCare's legal team prefers SCCs as the primary mechanism unless you can confirm DPF alignment for health-related context; speed is important, but we cannot compromise on legal equivalence.
- We need the full subprocessor list (including regional locations) for the set of services that touch any EU-origin data. Please flag any subprocessors that would require additional contractual commitments.
- Please provide the proposed DPA annex language. Our procurement team will use that as the starting point for redlines.

We've attached a set of internal RFP clarifications (zioncare_rfi_questions.pdf) — please call out anything that will materially change timelines. We're available for a 30-minute technical review on Tue 10/6 between 09:00-12:00 ET if you can make time.

Thanks again — Emily

Attachment: zioncare_rfi_questions.pdf
From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
To: Emily Roberts <emily.roberts@zioncare.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Data sovereignty & international transfers — ZionCare

Emily — attached is our consolidated response package and a draft DPA annex for your review. Highlights:

- Transfer mechanisms: Redwood supports SCCs in DPA annexes for patient-level data. For non-identifying telemetry and aggregated metrics we can apply the EU-US Data Privacy Framework where appropriate; we’ve documented the scope differences in the packet.
- Subprocessors: full roster included (with region flags). We’ve marked three subprocessors that will require additional contractual commitments (GPU partner, log aggregator, object store) — details are in section 3.
- Technical evidence: KMS key rotation policy, SOC2 summary, encryption diagrams, audit log retention statements, and sample audit entries.
- Deployment options: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved capacity + BYOK), Private (VPC/on-prem). For EU residency we recommend Dedicated or Private; the evidence packet includes the network egress controls for Dedicated clusters.

Attachments: redwood_evidence_pack.zip; dpa_annex_draft.docx

I've also created a Drive folder with full sources: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cZionRFI and a DocuSign link for the draft DPA if ZionCare wants to start execution in parallel: https://www.docusign.net/contract/abc123

We can take the 30-minute slot on Tue 10/6 at 09:30 ET — Marissa and Laura will join to walk through the packet. Please confirm and we'll send the calendar invite.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
